To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) drivers are more likely to push the limits of their vehicles and drive faster in races where the prize structure is more compressed (i.e., where the difference in prize money between first and second place is smaller) and (2) the effect of prize compression is stronger for drivers with lower career earnings and drivers who have won the race fewer times in their career.
